voiceover:
[conversational] One guy's IELTS essay checker makes about $5K a month, and he's selling it.

[curious] Stay till the end, because one pricing change is why it took off.

It's called Writing9. You submit an essay, and you get an estimated band score plus sentence-level corrections. Students pay $7.99 a week, $14.99 a month, or $29.99 a year.

These numbers are verified on TrustMRR: about $5K MRR, 587 active subscriptions, and about $100K all-time revenue. [serious] But it's down from its peak of around $12K a month, and he's selling it for $200K. Profit's hidden, so revenue isn't profit.

Founder Serhii Baraniuk failed his IELTS writing score several times, so he built the tool himself. No ads, just long-tail SEO. He shared the link with friends, and 3 days later someone bought a yearly plan.

Steal this: pick a narrow niche, win it with search, and build for a problem you've lived.

[whispers] Here's the move. He started at $5 a year with a 3-day trial. Then he switched to $10 a month, no trial. He says that's when sales took off.

[playful] Would you build this, or buy it for $200K?

pick.angle: A simple IELTS essay checker makes about $5K a month by fixing one painful problem for test-takers

research.what_it_does: An AI IELTS writing checker. You submit an essay, letter or chart description and get an estimated band score plus sentence-level corrections.
research.who_pays: IELTS test-takers (B2C students) who pay for a subscription for unlimited essay checks.
research.pricing: Homepage (writing9.com) lists Weekly $7.99/week, Monthly $14.99/month, Yearly $29.99/year. The yearly plan was shown as $37.49 crossed out with '20% off until the end of the week'. It also states a 100% money-back guarantee if you don't reach your target IELTS score. Premium includes unlimited submissions. An IELTSbiz review (Sept 2026) confirms the same three prices and says there is only a demo, no real free tier.
growth: Organic SEO. In his Starter Story interview the founder says he spent no money on ads. He focused on ranking for long-tail keywords, and that is how Writing9 grew (starterstory.com).

Launch was tiny. He shared the site link in a chat with friends who were also preparing for IELTS. Three days later the first person bought a yearly subscription, and the founder says it was still active five years on (Starter Story).

Pricing change drove sales. The first version cost $5 per year with a 3-day trial. He then switched to $10 per month with no trial. He says that change made sales take off and made the business profitable (Starter Story).
Homepage says 'Join 48,149 students who successfully passed IELTS' (writing9.com). This is a self-reported marketing claim, not independently verified.
founder_story: Serhii Baraniuk is a solo founder. Starter Story lists 1 founder and 0 employees. His X bio says 'solo founder' and lists several other products, plus '+11 failed'.
The idea came from his own struggle. He was preparing for IELTS and failed to get the required writing score several times (Starter Story).
He first built Writing9 on the side while working full-time as a programmer (Starter Story). It started in July 2018.
Starter Story says he is from Ukraine, and his X profile location says Barcelona.
lessons: Pick a narrow, high-intent niche (IELTS writing) and win it with long-tail SEO instead of paid ads. The founder credits this directly.
Don't underprice a high-stakes purchase. Moving from $5 per year with a trial to $10 per month with no trial is what he says made sales take off.
Build the tool for a problem you personally had. The founder lived the IELTS writing struggle.
criticism: Revenue is well below its peak. Starter Story and Venture Radar (about 455 days old) quoted about $12K–13K per month. TrustMRR now shows $4,778 MRR and $4,824 over the last 30 days, so it is much lower than when it was profiled.
The founder is selling the business for $200,000 (3.3x revenue). Profit is hidden on TrustMRR ('XX%'), so revenue is not profit.

Competitors say Writing9 scores less accurately than rivals. One rival's own benchmark (aat.ee, a competitor's self-published test) reported an average error of 1.62 band points for Writing9 against 0.49 for its own tool. A SmallTalk2Me comparison says scores can drift between submissions of the same essay. Treat both as competitor claims.
It covers Writing only, with no Speaking, Reading or Listening, and most features sit behind a paywall. Many AI IELTS checkers and free ChatGPT are alternatives.
Domain Rating is only 34/100 and the business depends heavily on Google search traffic.
facts: TrustMRR (Stripe-verified): MRR $4,778, 587 active subscriptions, $99,578 all-time revenue, 14% MoM growth, ~47,911 users, listed for $200,000.
Tech stack per TrustMRR: React, Express, MongoDB, Stripe.
Starter Story estimates the business makes about $156K per year at the time of the interview. This is a self-reported figure and is now outdated versus TrustMRR.
Homepage says the service can check Task 1 General letters, Task 1 Academic charts and Task 2 essays. It also says the final real exam score may differ slightly from the estimate.
do_not_claim: Profit or profit margin (hidden on TrustMRR).
Current team size beyond 'solo' as of the Starter Story interview.
That 48,149 students 'passed' IELTS because of it (marketing claim).
Any Product Hunt, Indie Hackers, X or viral launch. No source was found.
That the app is accurate to real examiner scores. Only competitor benchmarks exist, and they are negative.
Where the founder lives. Sources conflict: Barcelona, Odessa and United States.
Current pricing beyond the homepage snapshot. The yearly promo price may change.
research.notes: The homepage snippet I saw was cached (marked about 637 days old), so confirm the live pricing and the 'Join 48,149 students' counter when recording. The highlight phrases are copied from that cached text. Check the highlight text against the live page, especially '$29.99/year', since the promo styling may differ. I could not find individual feature, gallery or sample-essay pages, so only the homepage is listed. The strongest story angle is solo founder, SEO-only growth, a price change that unlocked sales, and now a drop from about $12K per month to about $4.8K MRR with the business for sale at $200K. Starter Story's headline is $12K per month, and TrustMRR's revenue is lower now. Describe it as 'down from its peak', not as growing, even though TrustMRR shows 14% MoM.
